property_summary: After the first fallback call (with 10 ether and block.timestamp > 0), P sets pastBlockTime to the current block timestamp; M reverts because pastBlockTime==0 fails, so pastBlockTime stays 0.

After a first call to fallback with 10 ether at block.timestamp=10, and a second call at a later block number where block.number % 15 == 0, the reference contract sends Ether to the caller and keeps pastBlockTime set, but the mutant reverts on the second call because it requires pastBlockTime == 0.

After an initial fallback call with 10 ether succeeds on the reference but reverts on the buggy version, address(c).balance is lower in the reference (because the transfer reduces it) than in the buggy version (where the revert leaves the balance unchanged).
